correctness.rationale: The exact Hintikka recursion with atomic equality and adjacency describes rank-four FO equivalence by induction. An exhaustive C++ enumeration of 3690 disconnected no-isolate linear forests below order 29 and 846 at 29 checks every path class by Brown–Hoshino Theorem 3.10. Only (14,15) at total order 29 matches. Independently coded bottom-up recursion reproduces the five positive boundary identities and salient negatives. The disjoint-union EF strategy transports all path lengths >=16 to the canonical size 16, closing every infinite parameter case. Isolated-vertex and one-vertex cases are separated by explicit rank-two formulas. Full limitations are stated.

originality.rationale: An exact two-component rank-four path-vs-disconnected-path criterion and the unique 29-vertex minimum are not stated or implied by the inspected Brown–Hoshino theorem, which compares only pairs of connected paths. The needed five disjoint-union type identities and the exhaustive minimality census are independently new finite calculations within the supplied evidence. Existing generic FO inexpressibility of connectedness does not imply these exact thresholds. Search and historical coverage is necessarily incomplete; the unpublished/technical Brown–Woodrow report is a named priority risk.

value.rationale: This solves the complete connected-versus-two-component equivalence problem for rank-four first-order logic on a canonical sparse family, and obtains a sharp, unique 29-vertex counterexample to finite-depth definability of connectedness among all linear forests. The threshold depends on the interaction between endpoint configurations and four-round alternation, is not implied by the 16-vertex connected-path stabilization alone, and supplies a reproducible exact benchmark for finite-model-theoretic methods. The result has natural invariant/size motivation without requiring a downstream theorem.
